description: Tasks for months 1-6 and beyond after a death

tasks.title: File the deceased's final tax return
tasks.description: File a final income tax return (Form 1040) for the deceased covering January 1 through the date of death. This is due by the normal April deadline.
tasks.why_it_matters: The final tax return is a legal requirement. It may result in a refund to the estate or identify taxes owed. The estate cannot be fully settled until taxes are resolved.
documents_needed: W-2s and 1099s for the year of death
Previous year's tax return for reference
Records of all income through date of death
tips: Write 'DECEASED' and the date of death across the top of Form 1040
The surviving spouse can file jointly for the year of death
Consider hiring a CPA experienced with estate taxes
File for an extension if you need more time (Form 4868)
Keep records—the IRS can audit estate returns for 3 years

tasks.title: Complete the probate process
tasks.description: If required, work through the probate court process to validate the will, settle debts, and legally transfer assets to beneficiaries.
tasks.why_it_matters: Probate gives the executor legal authority to act on behalf of the estate. It ensures debts are properly paid and assets legally transferred.
tips: Not all assets go through probate (joint accounts, beneficiary designations, trusts)
Small estates may qualify for simplified probate procedures
The executor may be entitled to compensation (varies by state)
Keep detailed records of all transactions and decisions
Probate typically takes 6-12 months, sometimes longer

tasks.title: Distribute assets per will or trust
tasks.description: Once debts are paid and probate permits, distribute remaining assets to beneficiaries according to the will or trust, or by state law if there's no will.
tasks.why_it_matters: This is the ultimate purpose of estate administration—ensuring your loved one's wishes are honored and beneficiaries receive their inheritance.
documents_needed: Release forms for beneficiaries to sign
tips: Get receipts or releases from beneficiaries for each distribution
Consider tax implications of distributing certain assets
Personal items with sentimental value can be the hardest—consider a family meeting
If beneficiaries disagree, a mediator may help
Keep reserves for any final taxes or unexpected expenses

tasks.title: Handle property sale (if applicable)
tasks.description: If the estate includes real property that will be sold, work with a real estate agent to list and sell the property. Ensure title is clear and proceeds go to the estate.
tasks.why_it_matters: Real estate is often the largest estate asset. A proper sale ensures maximum value and legal transfer. Proceeds are typically needed to settle the estate.
documents_needed: Letters Testamentary or court authority to sell
tips: Get the property appraised for estate tax purposes
Consider an estate sale for contents before listing
A real estate attorney can help with title issues
The estate may be responsible for maintenance until sold
Capital gains on inherited property are calculated from date-of-death value

tasks.title: Close remaining accounts
tasks.description: Close any remaining accounts in the deceased's name once the estate is settled. This includes bank accounts, investment accounts, and any remaining credit accounts.
tasks.why_it_matters: Closing accounts completes the financial wind-down of the estate and prevents any ongoing fees or potential fraud.
tips: Transfer remaining funds to the estate account before closing
Get confirmation letters that accounts are closed
Request final statements for record-keeping
Close investment accounts after distributing assets to beneficiaries
Keep estate bank account open until all distributions are complete

tasks.title: File estate tax return (if required)
tasks.description: If the estate exceeds the federal exemption ($12.92M in 2023, adjusted for inflation), file IRS Form 706. Some states have lower thresholds.
tasks.why_it_matters: Federal estate tax is 40% on amounts over the exemption. Missing the deadline can result in penalties and interest.
documents_needed: Complete inventory of all assets at fair market value
Appraisals for real estate, businesses, and valuables
Records of all deductions (debts, funeral expenses, etc.)
tips: Most estates don't owe federal estate tax (exemption is over $12M)
Some states have estate or inheritance taxes with lower thresholds
A CPA or estate attorney experienced in estate taxes is essential
Form 706 is due 9 months after death (extension available)
Portability allows surviving spouse to use unused exemption

tasks.title: Handle digital assets and online accounts
tasks.description: Close or memorialize social media accounts, cancel online subscriptions, and address email accounts and digital photos.
tasks.why_it_matters: Digital accounts can be targets for hackers. Memorializing social media preserves the profile while preventing login. Digital photos may be precious memories.
documents_needed: Any passwords or password manager access
tips: Facebook allows memorialization or deletion by verified family
Google has an Inactive Account Manager for planning ahead
Back up digital photos before closing any accounts
Check for any cryptocurrency wallets (may have significant value)
Some email providers will provide account contents to next of kin

tasks.title: Organize and store final estate records
tasks.description: Compile all estate documents, receipts, and records into organized files. Store securely for at least 7 years in case of audits or questions.
tasks.why_it_matters: Good records protect the executor from liability and answer questions that may arise later. Tax authorities can audit for years after.
tips: Keep copies of all filed tax returns
Maintain records of all distributions to beneficiaries
Store receipts for all expenses paid from the estate
Keep the final accounting submitted to the court
Consider both physical and digital backups
